notes: Genetically silencing V1 interneurons (Engrailed1-expressing inhibitory cells) eliminates fast motor bursting during locomotion, establishing local inhibition as the element that sets locomotor CPG cycle frequency and positioning V1 neurons as an evolutionarily conserved speed-control pathway for vertebrate locomotor movements.
animal_study: Test the claimed evolutionary conservation directly: silence V1-equivalent inhibitory populations in zebrafish or lamprey and test whether fast bursting selectively drops while slow rhythms persist, as in mouse.
robot_sim: Add an inhibitory V1-analog population to a half-center CPG whose gain sets burst frequency; ablating it should selectively remove fast motor bursting while slower rhythms persist, separating speed control from rhythm generation.

notes: Extensor and flexor premotor interneurons are segregated medio-laterally in the dorsal spinal cord yet derive from common progenitor domains separated only by timing of neurogenesis, and proprioceptive feedback selectively targets the medial extensor premotor population, where it is required for extensor-specific connectivity to develop — an anatomical and developmental basis for antagonistic circuitry.
animal_study: Neonatal dorsal-root section or genetic elimination of muscle spindles at different developmental stages, followed by trans-synaptic viral mapping of premotor connectivity, would test whether proprioceptive input is instructive for extensor premotor organization or merely permissive.
robot_sim: Route proprioceptive feedback preferentially onto the extensor premotor side of a bilateral CPG and remove it during connection formation to test whether extensor-specific connectivity fails to develop, mirroring the developmental requirement.
flags: Abstract attributes extensor premotor targeting to unnamed 'proprioceptive' feedback (no afferent class); feedback left empty — developmental targeting, no vocabulary fit.

notes: In a single-joint neuromechanical model, length (Ia, II) and extensor force (Ib) feedback entrain the CPG to limb dynamics and produce the extensor-dominated speed regulation of real locomotion — higher drive shortens stance while swing stays nearly constant, an asymmetry absent from the CPG's fictive pattern — and increasing afferent weights restores stable locomotion after supraspinal drive removal, mechanistically modeling locomotor training after spinal cord injury.
animal_study: Test the training prediction in spinal-transected animals: treadmill training with augmented versus reduced extensor load feedback (robotic stance loading, or deafferented controls) should speed or slow recovery of stepping, probing whether recovery acts through increased afferent input weights.
robot_sim: Implement the two-muscle single-joint CPG with Ia/II length and extensor Ib force feedback; sweep drive to verify stance-only shortening, ablate afferents to collapse speed regulation to the intrinsic fictive pattern, and raise afferent weights to emulate post-SCI training recovery.
flags: Model paper with ensemble Ia/II/Ib feedback modulating CPG phase durations; no vocabulary entry covers generic CPG entrainment by afferent feedback, so feedback left empty.

notes: Firing-map stability analysis of periodically forced integrate-and-fire oscillators yields the Arnold-tongue organization of p:q mode-locked states for sinusoidal, spike-train synaptic, and coupled-pair forcing — the standard framework for predicting when periodic input entrains a neural oscillator and when bursting (spike/quiescence) regimes emerge.
animal_study: Periodically stimulate an identified rhythmic neuron (intracellular sinusoidal current, or periodic afferent stimulation in an isolated spinal cord) and map firing ratios p:q across amplitude and frequency; observing Arnold-tongue structure would test the framework in real tissue.
robot_sim: Use firing-map/Arnold-tongue analysis to predict entrainment regimes of simulated CPG neurons under periodic afferent drive; verify mode-locked p:q states and bursting solutions against direct numerical simulation.

notes: A multi-expert learning architecture gates and blends pretrained deep-network experts and synthesizes new policies online, letting a single quadruped controller trot, steer, and recover from falls on real hardware — a machine-learning route to the adaptive multiskill locomotion that fixed CPG controllers lack.

Commissural interneurons organizing left-right hindlimb coordination form distinct rostral-lumbar flexor and extensor centers that define activity in caudal flexor and extensor motor pools across the midline, with some connections functionally reconfigured when switching from rest to locomotion — a candidate substrate for state-dependent spinal synaptic plasticity.
animal_study: Test whether the rest-to-locomotion reconfiguration of commissural connections is activity-dependent: pharmacologically block locomotor-like activity during the transition in the neonatal cord preparation and re-assess commissural inputs onto identified motor pools.
robot_sim: Implement distinct flexor and extensor commissural centers driving contralateral caudal motor pools, with connection weights that switch between rest and locomotion states; ablating the commissural population should collapse left-right alternation.

notes: Staggered thoracic lateral hemisections in cats shift the ipsilesional hindlimb from stance/extensor dominance toward swing/flexor while the contralateral limb compensates with prolonged stance and reduced swing, and forelimbs take extra steps independent of speed or lesion side — lesion signatures that reorganized sensorimotor network models must reproduce.
animal_study: Combine the staggered hemisections with dorsal-root deafferentation to test how much of the ipsilesional swing/stance rebalancing and contralateral stance compensation depends on afferent feedback versus reorganized central circuits, across walking speeds.
robot_sim: Model staggered hemisection as unilateral loss of descending drive plus partial crossed-connection removal in a quadruped CPG; test whether ipsilesional stance shortening, contralateral stance prolongation, and extra forelimb steps emerge without retuning, and how they scale with speed.

notes: Reviews Data Driven Floquet Analysis — fitting empirical return maps to the trajectories of rhythmic legged systems — and collects the recent and classical results that justify its use for analyzing legged locomotion where idealized periodicity assumptions fail.
animal_study: Apply DDFA to perturbed walking animals (brief treadmill speed steps or ground-height changes in cats) and test whether the empirically fitted Floquet modes predict recovery trajectories and stability limits.
robot_sim: Fit data-driven Floquet maps to joint-angle cycles from a simulated walker, extract mode structure and stability, and compare with the model's analytic eigenstructure — checking that simulation trajectories support the same empirical analysis as animal data.

notes: A two-mass, torque-actuated SLIP model with Coulomb-friction foot contact exhibits stable stick-slip periodic solutions in which low-friction slippage can increase average speed and reduce mechanical cost of transport, showing that ideal-sticking contact assumptions can misestimate both stability and energetics of legged locomotion.
animal_study: Measure cost of transport and preferred speed of animals or humans walking on low-friction versus normal surfaces, testing the counterintuitive prediction that tolerated slippage can improve energetic efficiency.
robot_sim: Implement the two-mass torque-actuated SLIP with Coulomb friction; sweep friction to locate stick-slip periodic solutions and test whether slippage regimes lower cost of transport and raise average speed.

notes: During quadrupedal locomotion in cats, forelimb movement modulates hindlimb cutaneous reflexes evoked by superficial peroneal stimulation, particularly the occurrence of long-latency responses — evidence that interlimb (forelimb-hindlimb) signals gate spinal cutaneous reflex pathways during walking.
animal_study: Externally drive forelimb movements in spinal-transected cats while stimulating the superficial peroneal nerve during hindlimb locomotion, testing whether the forelimb-dependent modulation of long-latency hindlimb reflexes survives transection and localizing the gating circuit.
robot_sim: Add forelimb-state-dependent gain modulation to hindlimb cutaneous reflex pathways in a quadruped neuromechanical model; ablating the modulation should remove the long-latency reflex gating present during quadrupedal walking.
flags: Forelimb-movement gating of hindlimb cutaneous long-latency reflexes has no vocabulary entry; feedback left empty.

notes: A hybrid controller pairing a Unit Burst Generator feedforward CPG with a small reflex set simulates physiological cycling across speeds and seat heights and transfers to walking after adding only a balance component, demonstrating that physiologically grounded CPG+reflex hybrids can generalize across cyclical lower-limb tasks instead of being task-specific.
animal_study: Perturb the crank or seat during human cycling and compare evoked reflex responses with the controller's feedback components, validating which reflex pathways are actually engaged in steady cycling and whether the same set carries over to walking.
robot_sim: Implement the Unit Burst Generator plus limited reflex set on a cycling musculoskeletal model; verify generalization across speeds and seat heights, ablate the reflex component to quantify its contribution, and add the balance module to test walking transfer.
flags: The abstract does not enumerate the reflex pathways in the feedback component; afferents and feedback left empty.

notes: Two parallel robot lines — cockroach-mimicking multi-segmented legs versus abstracted one-motor-per-tripod platforms whose gait changes emerge from passive mechanisms — establish that preflexive biomechanics can implement terrain-adaptive gait switching without neural control, capturing biological locomotion principles in deployable hardware.
animal_study: Test how much of the cockroach's terrain-dependent gait change survives neural silencing (anesthetized or nerve-cut preparations moving over obstacles), quantifying the preflexive-mechanical contribution that the passive robot designs posit.
robot_sim: Build an abstracted hexapod with passive gait-change mechanisms; lock or remove the passive degrees of freedom to measure how much terrain adaptation survives without them, isolating preflexive from neurally controlled contributions.

notes: A neuromusculoskeletal cat model with two-level half-center CPGs per hindlimb reproduces the adaptive interlimb coordination observed when spinalized cats suddenly lose ground support — without any parameter re-optimization — and nullcline analysis attributes the robustness to afferent feedback controlling the transitions between fast and slow neuronal dynamics.
animal_study: In spinalized cats trained to walk, deliver sudden ground-loss perturbations while selectively suppressing group I afferent conduction, testing the prediction that afferent control of fast-slow transitions — not re-tuned parameters — carries the adaptive interlimb response.
robot_sim: Implement paired two-level half-center CPGs whose fast-slow transitions are controlled by afferent feedback, tuned on flat ground only; drop the foot into a hole without re-optimization and check that adaptive interlimb coordination emerges, then analyze the transition nullclines.
flags: Afferent feedback controls fast-slow transition dynamics in the model, but the abstract names no afferent classes; feedback left empty.

notes: Blocking neurotransmission from excitatory V3 neurons (tetanus toxin) or acutely reducing their excitability destabilizes the locomotor rhythm, and V3 activity balances output between the two halves of the spinal cord — V3 neurons distribute excitatory drive bilaterally to keep the walking rhythm robust and left-right symmetric.
animal_study: Unilateral V3 silencing would directly test the proposed bilateral drive distribution, predicting left-right rhythm asymmetry or compensatory contralateral changes that bilateral blockade cannot resolve.
robot_sim: Add a bilaterally projecting excitatory V3-analog population distributing drive between the two half-centers; ablating it should produce an irregular, unbalanced rhythm without abolishing locomotion entirely.
flags: Abstract does not name the species; animals left empty rather than assumed.

notes: Letting the foot step into a hole reduces knee and ankle extensor activity to roughly 70% of normal in decerebrate cats, and selectively resisting ankle extension restores it; with segmental dorsal-root sections mapped accordingly, more than half of stance-phase extensor drive is proprioceptive — a continuous load-scaled contribution that automatically matches burst intensity to external demands.
animal_study: Selective inactivation of spindles versus tendon organs during stance (vibration, local anesthetic) combined with foot-in-hole trials would identify which proprioceptor class supplies the load-dependent extensor burst reinforcement.
robot_sim: Implement autogenic load-dependent extensor burst reinforcement during stance in a neuromechanical walker; removing ground support should cut extensor activity to about 70%, and resisting extension should restore it, directly testing the afferent share of stance drive.
flags: Extensor burst reinforcement is attributed to unnamed 'proprioceptors' (loading/unloading and dorsal-root manipulations — classic Ib autogenic excitation territory), but no afferent type is named; afferents and feedback left empty.

notes: V1 and V2b inhibitory interneurons act in opposition on flexor-extensor alternation: V1 ablation causes limb hyperflexion (V1-derived inhibition is needed for proper extension), while V2b loss causes hindlimb hyperextension and delays the stance-to-swing transition, with each class biased toward innervating flexor- versus extensor-related motoneurons.
animal_study: Combine V1 or V2b ablation with deafferentation to test whether the hyperflexion/hyperextension and the delayed stance-to-swing transition persist without sensory input, separating inhibitory gating deficits from afferent compensation.
robot_sim: Model V1 and V2b inhibitory populations with biased flexor/extensor motoneuron innervation; ablating V2b should reproduce hyperextension plus a delayed stance-to-swing transition, and ablating V1 hyperflexion.
flags: Abstract never names the species (V1/V2b ablation in awake behaving animals); animals left empty rather than assumed.

notes: Backward walking in cats reuses the forward reciprocal synergies — flexors in swing, extensors in stance — but retunes temporal parameters and amplitudes (gastrocnemius active from midswing with ramping stance EMG, near-absent knee and ankle yield, early-ending iliopsoas with prolonged semitendinosus), indicating one direction-general circuit with task-specific reweighting.
animal_study: Load and unload extensors during backward walking (as done for forward) or deafferent trained cats walking backward to quantify how much of the re-timed synergies depends on afferent feedback versus central reweighting.
robot_sim: Retune only burst timing and amplitude parameters of a single CPG-synergy controller to reproduce backward-walking EMG benchmarks (LG from midswing, ramping stance EMG, absent yield), testing whether one synergy set covers both directions with temporal reweighting alone.

notes: V2a interneurons are dispensable for left-right coordination at low locomotor frequencies but essential at high frequencies because rhythmic synaptic drive to a subpopulation grows with cycle frequency and recruits subthreshold oscillating V2a neurons — speed-dependent recruitment within one pool rather than activation of a silent second set.
animal_study: Record identified V2a neurons in vivo across treadmill speeds to confirm the frequency-dependent recruitment seen in vitro, and test whether left-right coordination errors at high gait speeds correlate with V2a recruitment failure.
robot_sim: Model a V2a pool whose subthreshold units recruit as rhythmic synaptic drive grows with cycle frequency; ablating it should degrade left-right coordination only at high frequencies while sparing low-frequency alternation.

notes: Bilateral infraorbital nerve section in head-fixed rats leaves the generation, patterning, and bilateral coordination of whisking intact, meeting the strict sensory-independence criteria for a whisking central pattern generator; unilateral section produces only a transient bilateral increase in whisking frequency.
animal_study: Locate the whisking CPG with serial transections combined with kinematic recording, or test pattern modulation after partial deafferentation using natural reafferent perturbations such as air puffs on the whiskers.
robot_sim: Remove all sensory feedback from a bilateral rhythmic model and verify that generation, patterning, and bilateral coordination persist — the deafferentation benchmark for CPG claims — and add a transient frequency elevation after unilateral feedback loss to match the behavioral result.
flags: Whisking rhythm survives bilateral deafferentation — conceptually 'Fictive locomotion without sensory feedback' but for whisking rather than locomotion; feedback left empty pending Ben's call.

notes: In chronic spinal cord injury, hip movement direction gates reflexes at the knee and ankle — patellar tendon reflexes are larger during hip extension and the tonic Achilles vibration response larger during hip flexion — while knee and ankle afferent input leaves hip-triggered reflexes unchanged, giving hip stretch afferents a privileged modulatory role over the whole leg.
animal_study: Test hip afferent priority in a reduced preparation: oscillate the hip in decerebrate cats while eliciting patellar and Achilles reflexes, checking whether hip position similarly gates distal reflexes as in human SCI.
robot_sim: Make knee and ankle reflex gains in a leg model depend on hip angle (larger patellar gain during extension, larger tonic vibration response during flexion); ablate the dependence to test its role in spastic-reflex modulation.
flags: Hip-position-dependent gating of knee/ankle stretch reflexes has no vocabulary entry; afferent types not named; feedback left empty.

notes: A bipedal robot with strap actuators, Golgi-tendon-organ-like strap load sensors, and a spiking half-center CPG with phase-modulated reflexes walks with the cycle entrained to body dynamics, and the CPG stabilizes gait against perturbations beyond a purely reflexive controller — a physical test of CPG-reflex synergy benchmarked against human walking trajectories.
animal_study: Compare perturbation recovery in intact versus deafferented walking animals to quantify the stabilizing contribution the robot attributes to the CPG — the reflex-only versus CPG+reflex contrast predicts smaller recovery margins after deafferentation.
robot_sim: Replicate in simulation: half-center CPG plus phase-modulated reflexes with Ib strap-force feedback on a biped; ablate the CPG to leave reflex-only control and quantify the stability loss against matched perturbations.

notes: A spiking neuron model combining a nonresetting leaky integrator with a multi-timescale adaptive threshold reproduces and predicts diverse spike responses — regular spiking, intrinsic bursting, fast spiking, and chattering — with only three adaptive threshold parameters, expressing firing characteristics as a continuum rather than discrete classes at low computational cost.
animal_study: Fit the three adaptive-threshold parameters to intracellular recordings of identified spinal interneurons and validate predicted responses to fluctuating current injection, testing the made-to-order claim on locomotor rather than cortical neurons.
robot_sim: Use the multi-timescale adaptive-threshold IF unit as a low-cost spiking neuron class in CPG networks; sweep its three parameters across regular-spiking to intrinsic-bursting regimes and measure how heterogeneous unit classes influence network rhythm properties.

notes: Mice lacking Wt1 in neurons run slower with decreased stride frequency and increased stride length, show altered fore-hindlimb coordination accompanied by loss of contralateral spinal projections, and display arrhythmic reduced-frequency motor output as neonates — tying a Wt1-expressing dI6 subpopulation to left-right coordination circuitry assembly.
animal_study: Test whether the coordination deficits are afferent-dependent: run Wt1 mutants on a treadmill with perturbations, or evoke locomotion pharmacologically in neonatal spinal cords while recording ventral roots, separating circuit miswiring from sensory reweighting.
robot_sim: Reduce contralateral commissural projection weights in a bilateral CPG to mimic Wt1 loss; check for slower cadence, longer strides, degraded interlimb coordination, and arrhythmic motor output.

notes: The Drosophila peristaltic-crawling circuitry assembles into a functional central pattern generator with no sensory input at all, but sensory information is required to integrate the circuit into actual locomotion: without afferent input, movement polarity is deranged and backward peristaltic waves predominate at the expense of forward peristalsis.
animal_study: Restore individual sensory modalities in sensory-null embryos (class-specific mechanoreceptor rescue) to determine which afferent inputs re-establish forward-polarity peristalsis, identifying the polarity-determining sensory signal.
robot_sim: Assemble a peristaltic-crawling CPG with zero afferent feedback and verify the rhythm self-organizes; then add sensory feedback to control wave polarity, ablating it to reproduce the backward-dominant peristalsis seen without afferents.

notes: A robotic-fish controller in which sensory feedback reshapes CPG coupling topology and parameters online — with a finite-state machine selecting among swimming gaits — improves maneuverability and adaptability in simulation and underwater tests, an engineering demonstration of feedback-driven CPG reconfiguration for multimodal locomotion.
robot_sim: Implement a CPG whose coupling forms and control parameters are shaped online by sensory feedback under finite-state gait selection; test multimodal gait switching and adaptation to environmental change against fixed-coupling CPGs.
